small_guidance:
- The conv dominates runtime here (B=1024, output spatial = 13×29×29 ≈ 10933 elements per (n,c)). The fused post-conv kernel is fine; tuning BLOCK_S/num_warps further won't close the gap. Still, try BLOCK_S=512 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3 to better amortize the reduction over S≈10933.
- Add a `triton.autotune` over BLOCK_S ∈ {128, 256, 512, 1024} × num_warps ∈ {4, 8} keyed on (B, C, S) so the post-conv kernel is at least optimal.
- Fold the conv bias into the hardswish input path implicitly by ensuring `x` is already contiguous in (B,C,S); current `.contiguous().view` is fine but consider channels-last on the conv output to coalesce the per-(b,group) loads across S.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC_tile, output-spatial tile), with implicit im2col gather. With in_channels=3, kernel=4³=64, K=192 is small — pick BLOCK_K=64 (full K in 3 iters or one pass with BLOCK_K=192 padded), BLOCK_M (OC)=16 (full OC), BLOCK_N (spatial)=128, num_warps=4. This is the dominant cost and the highest-headroom target.
- Fuse hardswish + GroupNorm reduction (sum, sumsq, per-channel sum) directly into the conv kernel's epilogue: each conv tile writes per-channel partial sums into a (B, C) scratch and (B, G) sum/sumsq scratch using atomics, then a tiny second kernel finalizes mean/rstd and produces (B, C). This removes the separate read pass over the (B, C, 10933) conv output entirely.
- Alternatively, since C=16 is tiny and S≈10933 is large, persist the entire per-(N, OC) output tile in registers/SMEM within the conv kernel and do the hardswish + group reductions in-place before writing only the final (B, C) result — never materializing the (B, C, D, H, W) tensor. Grid = (B,), one program per batch row computes the full conv + norm + mean.
